top.line: Three scenarios, mapped, show where decisions go unwritten
top.para: The fourth article maps three scenarios, giving each element a policy and four states. Memory deletion in Mondweep's Ruflo adapter is enforced but unrecorded, with its approval undefined; this newsroom shipped every release with a pre-existing failing test, an unwritten decision; and an illustrative refund catches a limit-widening workflow before it runs.

in-short.line: Behaviour is enforced; the gaps are unwritten decisions
in-short.para: Each element gets a policy and four states. Memory deletion is blocked but its approver is unnamed and nothing logs the block; the newsroom's gap is shipping with one inherited failing test on judgement alone. Two small cases emerged, while the refund's tool limits catch a widening workflow, and naming an element makes its gap visible.

how.line: A map can be complete before the wiring
how.para: The series separates behaviour, decision and workflow policies, and gives each element four states: defined (written, with an owner), implemented, enforced (stopped by something outside the agent) and observed. The tables show them as D · I · E · O. A gap you have named is a gap you can decide about.

memory.line: Memory deletion is enforced, but nobody approves or records
memory.para: In Mondweep Chakravorty's adapter, delete.memory.project is in the ABP and enforced by Ruflo's evaluator, refused in step 6 of the video, but no decision is logged. The barrier says a human must approve without naming who or on what evidence, so approval means stop. Add a decision log first, then a named decider, then the workflow.

newsroom.line: Shipping past a failing test was an unwritten decision
newsroom.para: The agent pushes only to dev, a platform boundary, through a mostly scripted release recipe. In eight builds today it shipped past an inherited Portugal wire map test failure on its own judgement, which should be a written policy with an owner, a limit and an expiry. Two cases followed: an unchecked figure date and a mis-scoped leak-scan counter.

refund.line: Numeric tool limits catch a widening workflow before running
refund.para: In an illustrative design, tools cap refunds at the order value and 100 GBP, once per order, with a 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker, and a team lead then finance approve larger ones, though approvals leave no reasons behind. A well-meant VIP workflow refunding 1,000 GBP widens the limit, so a mechanical check fails it before it runs.

common.line: Behaviour is mature; decisions and observation lag behind
common.para: Across all three, behaviour is the easiest to write and enforce. The gaps are in decisions: no named approver for memory, an unwritten newsroom decision, approvals without reasons for refunds. Observation lags enforcement, since a rule that leaves no trace cannot be shown to work, and naming each element is what makes the gaps visible.

series.line: Four articles, ending with these three mapped decisions
series.para: The series runs from Three policies for an agent, on behaviour, decision and workflow, through Approve at altitude and its narrow-never-widen rule, to Case law for agents on precedent and distinguishing. Three decisions, mapped is the fourth and final part.

limits.line: A simulated refund, and states assessed rather than tested
limits.para: The refund is a simulation and no refunds were made. The states are my assessment, for the memory scenario from reading Mondweep's code rather than running it. Shipping with the failing test was reasonable, only unwritten, and the two flagged commits leaked nothing because they sat in scratch repositories never pushed anywhere.

sources.line: Sources: Mondweep's code, release records and an earlier design
sources.para: Scenario 1 draws on mondweep/sgit-ruv-memory at 7607d72, its example ABP and the page merged into ruvnet/ruflo on 17 October 2026. Scenario 2 uses the newsroom's release record, v0.12.89 to v0.12.97, with build and test logs and the status report. Scenario 3 builds on Hope or enforcement, with illustrative approval levels.
